title: Racial hatred, family prejudice and neighborly loyalty in New Orleans
summary: Albert and Dick discuss racial animosity, color feeling among families, and neighbor loyalty. His grandmother as midwife delivered many white babies.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: Well what about your family? How do they feel about people? Different kinds of people.

Well the old tradition around here has changed considerably but there always was that bridge between families. The old feud and families then into the some didn't like the dark complected ones, the dark complected ones, but vice versa. They didn't like the brides or the whites. It was always. As far as I'm concerned this racial problem has always been. It has always been the same thing. The hatred seems to be instilled in people in this. I don't know whether I can truthfully say that time is going to eliminate that. I doubt seriously that. It's always going to be that element that is going to be retained within a fellow about hatred or animosity against someone else. If it's something he doesn't like about the fellow, he is going to hold that against it.
I find a lot of that is not really racial. That's just an excuse to be nasty.
Right, but I've got to agree to that also.
Yeah, I mean, there's some people that are just going to be hateful and hate other people. They're mad at the

and they always going to find some excuse. But I find there's always been different kinds of people than you are. From steady, you know, and they have people who stand by other people. Some people are shy, some people are friendly.

Well, yes, that's a common way of life here in New Orleans. it's been that way as far back as I can remember. But I tell you one thing that I find this that still exists. The loyalty among relatives and close friends and neighbors, that still exists in certain parts. Because just for instance, if a neighbor say there's someone taken sick in the family, it wouldn't be ten minutes before half of the neighborhood being there trying to see what they could do. Which I think is great. And for instance, my grandmother was a midwife. And I guess my grandmother brought more white people in the world than she did me was. As a politician here, I was raised up with his name a scammer. But my grandmother brought him into the world and she brought all of his kids. The hatred and the prejudices, I don't think existed as much in those days, but the little frictions were there.
